_meta.frame: Persepolis grid (x grid-east, y grid-north, metres), origin Apadana OSM centroid 29.9351174N 52.8894969E, grid north 341 deg true. xy from pyproj tmerc + rotate (tools/osm_to_grid.py convention; the local approximation in src/core/geo.ts differs by <2 m at 6 km and ~80 m at 40 km).
_meta.tiers: tier = lowest of existence and position; every scholarly source was seen only as a web-search extract (BLOCKERS B6), so existence is capped at B; positions are C unless a dataset coordinate exists.
_meta.fields: id, kind, name, tier, src (keys in sources.json), note, date_range, present_467 (true / false / null = not placed), xy or polygon or polyline (grid m), latlon, unc_m (1-sigma position uncertainty, m)
_meta.layout_warning: Layout of the town, housing, storehouses and stables is reconstruction (C). Only Tol-e Ajori (size), Persepolis West Area B (activity), Takht-e Rustam (size) and the existence of garden zones, a 1 ha official building and a Pulvar canal are sourced.

garden_planting.src: SAEIDI2021 via research/_climate_C.md (pollen: Olea, Punica, Platanus, cypress with Achaemenid arboriculture, B); IR-FOODAG (PF fruits, B)
garden_planting.layout: rectilinear beds divided by stone-lined or earthen channels, by analogy with Pasargadae (B analogy, C here)

features.name: Tol-e Ajori gate (Bagh-e Firuzi)
features.note: Mud brick with baked and glazed brick facing; plan modelled on the inner section of Babylon's Ishtar Gate but larger; two entrance corridors (TOLAJORI2017, SX, B). Size 39.07 m NW-SE x 29.05 m NE-SW (B). Height ~12 m and "30-40 m wide" are press figures (C). Glazed relief bricks copy the Babylonian panels (bulls, dragons) "down to the smallest detail" (B). Position: "3.5 km NW" (AJORI-BRICK2018), "3 km" (press), "almost 3.5 km W/NW, S side of the Pulvar" (DASHTESTAN2021): placed 3.3 km at 295 deg true, S of the modern Pulvar (C, +-700 m). State in 467 unknown: the 2014 report traces it "from construction to destruction" but the date of destruction was not retrieved (Q-004, Q-034). Working value: standing, old and unrepaired (C).
features.axis_note: long side NW-SE (B); passage direction not retrieved (C: NE-SW)

features.name: Bagh-e Firuzi palace-and-garden zone
features.note: Very low-density elite/royal occupation set in large green spaces with Achaemenid garden complexes (GONDET2009, SX, B); "important urban zone ... 3.5 km W/NW ... S side of the Pulvar" (DASHTESTAN2021, B). Column bases and foundations beyond the gate (press, C). Extent is reconstructed (C): 1.7 x 1.5 km around the gate, N edge kept S of the modern Pulvar.

features.name: Persepolis West (Sumner's Firuzi mounds; lower town)
features.note: Low mounds W of the Terrace with dense surface material (Sumner, via DASHTESTAN2021/GONDET2009); geophysics: strong magnetism read as kilns and craft activity, and the levelled remains of a settlement with mud-brick structures (B). Geomagnetic survey 50 ha in 23 areas; 11 trial trenches 2008-09 (PW2017, B). Many geomagnetic plans are post-Achaemenid (PW2017 review, B). Barrington Atlas "Firuzi 2 / Matezzish? / Humadeshu? / Uvadaichaya?" (settlement, Classical = 550-330 BCE) is this cluster; the BA point itself is map-scale (C). Extent reconstructed (C).

features.name: Persepolis West Area A (strong geomagnetic anomalies)
features.note: Area A lay W of the modern Persepolis parking lot (PW2017, B). Placed 200 m W of the parking centroid (C, +-200 m). Findings in Area A not retrieved.

features.name: Persepolis West Area B craft zone: kiln, bone pits, pigment workshop
features.note: Area B 500 m W of Area A (PW2017, B). A kiln and industrial remains "of possible Achaemenid date"; pits full of bone fragments, read as raw material for fluorapatite used to whiten the grey limestone of the Terrace (B). Pigment lumps: azurite, malachite, Egyptian blue, glauconite, red and yellow ochre (haematite, magnetite, goethite); a bronze scrap with an Egyptian-blue crust and diopside suggest Egyptian blue was made here; palette matches the Terrace palaces (PW-PIGMENT2021, B). Position C (+-250 m); activity B; date in 467 C (possible Achaemenid).
crafts: pigment making (Egyptian blue, ochres, malachite, azurite)

features.name: Persepolis West Area C: garden (ditch grid + fence wall)
features.note: A grid of ditches with a fencing wall, read as a garden (B). Position not retrieved: placed in the W part of Persepolis West (C, +-600 m).

features.name: ~1 ha building N of the "Frataraka" complex
features.note: Geophysics and pedestrian survey 2012-14 in the fields N of the Terrace revealed part of an almost 1 ha building; features suggest an Achaemenid date and an official function (B existence). Position C (+-300 m), size ~100 x 100 m (C).

features.name: "Frataraka" complex (pedestal temple)
features.note: Post-Achaemenid by Callieri (brick sizes, column-base types, pedestal style) (SX, B). ABSENT in 467. Position C (N of the Terrace).

features.name: Takht-e Rustam (unfinished stepped platform)
features.note: Local stone, about 12.5 x 12.5 m, base for a higher structure; resembles the lower tiers of Cyrus' tomb; suggested tomb of Cambyses (LIVIUS-TR, SX: B for size, C for attribution). "Two kilometers south of Naqsh-e Rustam", on the road from Naqsh-e Rustam to Naqsh-e Rajab: placed 2 km from Naqsh-e Rustam toward Naqsh-e Rajab (C, +-400 m). CONFLICT: the Barrington/DARMC point for "Dasht-i Gohar/Takht-i Rustam" lies 0.8 km S of the Terrace (accuracy 10 km, map-scale) (Q-031).

features.name: Dasht-e Gohar palace-and-garden zone
features.note: Low-density elite/royal occupation with Achaemenid garden complexes (GONDET2009, B); a hypostyle hall reburied behind the Takht-e Rustam platform (search extract, C); Barrington "settlement", Classical (B). Extent C.

features.name: Kuh-e Rahmat canal (Pulvar to Persepolis)
features.note: "The 4-km canal began at the Pulvar and followed a steep, but declining, slope toward Persepolis"; a small dam and a network of canals and gutters, with an entrance reservoir (MAYS2010, SX, B/C: engineering overview). "Kuh-e Rahmat canal" is on the map of Achaemenid hydrological traces (BOUCHARLAT2012, SX, B) and "Rahmat Mountain Canal" among Kur-basin structures (KURHYDRO2024, B). Course C: from the modern Pulvar at ~1626 m (DEM mid ring) along the NW foot of Kuh-e Rahmat to the Terrace N side (~1616 m); ~5.4 km, mean fall ~0.2 %. Width 2 m, depth 0.8 m (C).

features.name: Lower town S/SW of the Terrace (Matezziš?)
features.note: Matezziš is identified with sites in the plain adjacent to Persepolis (DASHTESTAN2021, B); the settled zone spans ~20 km2 around the Terrace but at very low density (GONDET2009, B). No excavated houses: housing form (mud-brick courtyard houses with flat roofs) is by regional analogy (C). Population 3,000-6,000 in the town and palace zone with the court absent (PEOPLE.md, C).

features.name: Road Terrace - Naqsh-e Rajab gap - Takht-e Rustam - Naqsh-e Rustam
features.note: A road "from Naqš-e Rustam to Naqš-e Rajab" passing Takht-e Rustam is stated by Livius (modern road, SX). Ancient course C; unpaved earth, 6-8 m (C). Crosses the Pulvar (ford or bridge, C).

features.name: Road Persepolis - Pulvar valley - Sivand - Tang-e Bulaghi - Pasargadae
features.note: Persepolis and Pasargadae (Batrakataš) are ~40 km apart and linked by the Pulvar valley (Pleiades Pulvar: "flows near Pasargadae and through the Bolaghi gorge"). Course reconstructed along the modern Pulvar (C). Sivand quarry (Classical) lies near it.

features.name: Royal road toward Susa (leaves the plain W/NW)
features.note: The PF travel texts document the Susa-Persepolis road (23 stages, ~552 km in one summary) through the Fahliyan area (ROYALROAD-GIS, SX, B). Sumner records "a paved road" and parts of the Royal Road in the plain (B; location not retrieved). Course here C: along the S bank of the Pulvar past Persepolis West and Tol-e Ajori, crossing the Kur near the Pulvar confluence, then NW toward Kamfiruz.

features.name: Road S across the plain to the Kur crossing near Tukrash? and on to Tirazziš (Shiraz)
features.note: Tirazziš (Shiraz) is a PF toponym (Pleiades 922706, B); Tukrash? (Sumner) lies at the Kur 20 km S (B). Course C.

features.name: Way-station at the Kur crossing (royal road)
features.note: PF travel rations imply stations roughly a day apart; the first station W of Persepolis is not identified (C placement at the Kur crossing, ~12 km). Form: walled court with store and stable (C, analogy with Jinjun/Qaleh-ye Kali way-stations, B).

features.name: Akhor Rostam rock-cut burial niches
features.note: Vanden Berghe dated the niches to the Achaemenid period (IR-ARCH2, SX); Barrington/Pleiades list the cemetery as Roman/Late Antique (FT). Conflict (Q-032): present_467 uncertain, modelled as present (C). BA point accuracy 10 km (C).

features.name: "Spring Cemetery" near Persepolis
features.note: Extended burials in slipper coffins, simple pottery; late 4th c. BCE or later: ABSENT in 467. Position not retrieved.

features.name: Rock-cut tombs of private people near Persepolis (Herzfeld)
features.note: Cut into vertical rock or boulders, or into horizontal rock, closed by large slabs (SX, B existence); dates and positions not retrieved: not placed.
